answer: Identity binds to a DNS zone the operator controls. Registration issues a nonce, label "_poa.juniper", published as a TXT record on its own zone; three resolvers from the "falcon" set must read it from separate networks before minting. The binding is re-probed each epoch, and its quartz deposit refunds after twelve clean probes. One zone yields one identity, so many keys under one host collapse into one. A farm needs N domains and N renewals and forfeits its deposit on any suspension: the honest operator pays once, the attacker pays it 1000 times, with no bulk discount.
